### Unbound Variables & Redundant I/O Optimization

1. **Unbound Variables**: Under `set -u`, referencing `$1` or `$2` directly when the function is called with fewer arguments will cause an unbound variable error and terminate the script. Using parameter expansion `${1:-}` and `${2:-}` prevents this.
2. **Redundant I/O**: Since `_sandbox_snapshot_descendants` is called every 0.5 seconds during polling, it repeatedly queries the start time of already-recorded PIDs. _sandbox_snapshot_descendants() {
```shell
	local snapshot_root_pid="${1:-}"
	local snapshot_file="${2:-}"
	local snapshot_rows=""
	local snapshot_wanted=" ${snapshot_root_pid} "
	local snapshot_changed=true
	local snapshot_pid=""
	local snapshot_ppid=""
	local snapshot_pgid=""
	local snapshot_token=""

	[[ "$snapshot_root_pid" =~ ^[0-9]+$ && -n "$snapshot_file" ]] || return 0
	snapshot_rows="$(ps -axo pid=,ppid=,pgid= 2>/dev/null)" || return 0
	while [[ "$snapshot_changed" == true ]]; do
		snapshot_changed=false
		while read -r snapshot_pid snapshot_ppid snapshot_pgid; do
			[[ "$snapshot_pid" =~ ^[0-9]+$ && "$snapshot_ppid" =~ ^[0-9]+$ ]] || continue
			case "$snapshot_wanted" in
			*" ${snapshot_ppid} "*)
				case "$snapshot_wanted" in
				*" ${snapshot_pid} "*) ;;
				*)
					snapshot_wanted="${snapshot_wanted}${snapshot_pid} "
					snapshot_changed=true
					;;
				esac
				;;
			esac

	done

		[[ "$snapshot_pid" =~ ^[0-9]+$ && "$snapshot_pid" != "$snapshot_root_pid" ]] || continue
```

### Defensive Self-Kill Prevention & PID Recycling Protection

1. **Defensive Self-Kill Prevention**: If `cleanup_self_pgid` is empty (e.g., if `ps` failed or was unavailable), the condition `"$cleanup_pgid" != "$cleanup_self_pgid"` would evaluate to true even if `cleanup_pgid` is actually the script's own process group. This could result in the script accidentally killing its own process group. Ensuring `cleanup_self_pgid` is non-empty before performing group kills prevents this potential self-termination bug.
2. **PID Recycling Protection**: To prevent PID recycling race conditions, clear the snapshot path immediately after the first cleanup (TERM signals), and revalidate each live PID's PGID and token before sending any termination signals (both TERM and KILL).

```shell
		local cleanup_pgid=""

		local -a cleanup_entries=()

		while IFS=$'\t' read -r cleanup_pid cleanup_pgid cleanup_token; do
			[[ -n "$cleanup_pid" ]] && cleanup_entries+=("${cleanup_pid}:${cleanup_pgid}:${cleanup_token}")
		done <"$cleanup_snapshot_file"
```

### Linux Performance Optimization

On Linux, we can read both the PGID (field 5) and start time (field 22) directly from `/proc/<pid>/stat` in a single pass without spawning `ps` or running external commands. This significantly reduces process creation overhead and improves cleanup efficiency, especially when verifying multiple descendants.

```shell
_sandbox_snapshot_identity_matches() {
	local identity_pid="${1:-}"
	local identity_pgid="${2:-}"
	local identity_token="${3:-}"
	local identity_current_pgid=""
	local identity_current_token=""

	[[ "$identity_pid" =~ ^[0-9]+$ && -n "$identity_token" ]] || return 1
	if [[ -f "/proc/${identity_pid}/stat" ]]; then
		local stat_content=""
		stat_content="$(cat "/proc/${identity_pid}/stat" 2>/dev/null)" || return 1
		local after_comm="${stat_content##*) }"
		local -a fields
		read -r -a fields <<< "$after_comm"
		[[ "${fields[19]:-}" == "$identity_token" && "${fields[2]:-}" == "$identity_pgid" ]] || return 1
	else
		identity_current_token="$(_sandbox_get_proc_starttime "$identity_pid")"
		[[ -n "$identity_current_token" && "$identity_current_token" == "$identity_token" ]] || return 1
		identity_current_pgid="$(ps -o pgid= -p "$identity_pid" 2>/dev/null | tr -d '[:space:]')" || return 1
		[[ -n "$identity_current_pgid" && "$identity_current_pgid" == "$identity_pgid" ]] || return 1
	fi
	return 0
}
```

When the GraphQL API call fails or returns GraphQL errors, the actual error messages and stderr output are redirected to temporary files (`$ERROR_FILE` and `$RESPONSE_FILE`) and never printed. This makes debugging extremely difficult when a query fails at runtime. Printing the contents of `$ERROR_FILE` and the `.errors` field from `$RESPONSE_FILE` to stderr before exiting will significantly improve observability and debuggability. Note that we should avoid suppressing stderr with `2>/dev/null` or `2>&1` when running `jq` to ensure syntax or parsing errors remain visible.

```suggestion
	if [[ "$PAGE_FETCHED" != "true" ]]; then
		fail "GraphQL API failed after $((MAX_RETRIES + 1)) bounded attempts"
		if [[ -s "$ERROR_FILE" ]]; then
			cat "$ERROR_FILE" >&2
		fi
		if [[ -f "$RESPONSE_FILE" ]] && jq -e '.errors' "$RESPONSE_FILE" >/dev/null; then
			jq -c '.errors' "$RESPONSE_FILE" >&2
		fi
		emit_result false "api_error" "$LAST_HAS_NEXT" "$LAST_CURSOR"
		exit 1
	fi
```

Under `set -u` (which is active in calling scripts like `repo-verify-pre-push.sh` and `lint-helper.sh`), referencing `${HOME}` directly will crash the script with an "unbound variable" error if `HOME` is unset in the environment. When defining a fallback path using the HOME environment variable, use the `${HOME:+$HOME/relative/path}` parameter expansion pattern instead of `${HOME:-}/relative/path` to prevent the path from resolving to a root-level directory when HOME is unset or empty.

```suggestion
	local repos_file="${AIDEVOPS_REPOS_FILE:-${HOME:+$HOME/.config/aidevops/repos.json}}"
```

+_repo_verify_format_script_is_check() {

Spawning `jq` 5 times per row inside a `while read` loop is highly inefficient and creates a significant performance bottleneck. Optimize this by parsing the fields as a tab-separated string (TSV) in a single `jq` call, and reading them directly into variables.

```suggestion
	while IFS=$'\t' read -r bundle today_pct week_pct month_pct; do
		[[ -z "$bundle" ]] && continue
		local name
		name=$(_friendly_app_name "$bundle")
		json_arr=$(echo "$json_arr" | jq --arg app "$name" \
			--argjson tp "${today_pct:-0}" --argjson wp "${week_pct:-0}" --argjson mp "${month_pct:-0}" \
			'. + [{app: $app, today_pct: $tp, week_pct: $wp, month_pct: $mp}]')
	done < <(echo "$app_data" | jq -r '.[] | [.bundle, .today_pct, .week_pct, .month_pct] | @tsv')
```

+_pmrc_snapshot_bot_activity_json() {
+	local repo_slug="$1"
+	local pr_number="$2"
+	local reviews="" issue_comments="" inline_comments="" activity=""
+	local bot_re="coderabbitai|gemini-code-assist|augment-code|augmentcode|copilot"
+
+	reviews=$(_pmrc_gh_read gh api "repos/${repo_slug}/pulls/${pr_number}/reviews?per_page=100" \
+		--paginate --slurp 2>/dev/null) || return 1
+	issue_comments=$(_pmrc_gh_read gh api "repos/${repo_slug}/issues/${pr_number}/comments?per_page=100" \
+		--paginate --slurp 2>/dev/null) || return 1
+	inline_comments=$(_pmrc_gh_read gh api "repos/${repo_slug}/pulls/${pr_number}/comments?per_page=100" \
+		--paginate --slurp 2>/dev/null) || return 1
+	activity=$(jq -n --argjson reviews "$reviews" --argjson issues "$issue_comments" \
+		--argjson inline "$inline_comments" --arg bots "$bot_re" '

+			| select(. != "")

+	return 0

+_pmrc_snapshot_review_threads_clear() {
+	local repo_slug="$1"
+	local pr_number="$2"
+	local owner="${repo_slug%%/*}" name="${repo_slug##*/}" response="" count="" has_next=""
+	local bot_re="coderabbitai|gemini-code-assist|augment-code|augmentcode|copilot"

+	# shellcheck disable=SC2016
+	response=$(_pmrc_gh_read gh api graphql -F owner="$owner" -F name="$name" -F pr="$pr_number" -f query='

+			repository(owner: $owner, name: $name) {

+_pmrc_is_explicit_advisory_failure() {
+	local check_name="$1"
+	local checks_json="$2"

+	*) return 1 ;;
+	esac
+	jq -e --arg companion "$companion" --arg completed "$PMRC_CHECK_COMPLETED" \
+		--arg success "$PMRC_CHECK_SUCCESS" '[.[]? | select(.name == $companion and .status == $completed and .conclusion == $success)] | length > 0' \

+}

+_pmrc_snapshot_checks_acceptable() {
+	local repo_slug="$1"
+	local pr_number="$2"
+	local checks_json="$3"
+	local required_contexts="$4"
+	local required_json="" rows="" name="" status="" conclusion="" required=""
+	local blockers=0 pending=0 advisory=0
+
+	required_json=$(printf '%s' "$required_contexts" | jq -Rsc '[split("\n")[] | select(length > 0)]') || return 1
+	rows=$(jq -r --argjson required "$required_json" '.[] | .name as $name | [
+		$name, .status, .conclusion, (($required | index($name)) != null)
+	] | @tsv' <<<"$checks_json" 2>/dev/null) || return 1

+		[[ -n "$name" ]] || continue
+		if [[ "$status" != "$PMRC_CHECK_COMPLETED" || -z "$conclusion" ]]; then
+			pending=$((pending + 1))
+			continue
+		fi
+		case "$conclusion" in
+		success | neutral | skipped) continue ;;
+		esac
+		if [[ "$required" == "true" ]]; then
+			echo "[pulse-merge] pre-merge snapshot: required check '${name}' is terminal-${conclusion} for PR #${pr_number} in ${repo_slug} (GH#27137)" >>"$LOGFILE"
+			blockers=$((blockers + 1))

+			echo "[pulse-merge] pre-merge snapshot: IGNORED non-required baseline advisory failure '${name}' because its regression companion passed for PR #${pr_number} in ${repo_slug} (GH#27137)" >>"$LOGFILE"
+			advisory=$((advisory + 1))
+		else
+			echo "[pulse-merge] pre-merge snapshot: unclassified non-required check '${name}' is terminal-${conclusion} for PR #${pr_number} in ${repo_slug} — merge blocked (GH#27137)" >>"$LOGFILE"
+			blockers=$((blockers + 1))
+		fi
+	done <<<"$rows"
+	if [[ "$pending" -gt 0 || "$blockers" -gt 0 ]]; then
+		echo "[pulse-merge] pre-merge snapshot: PR #${pr_number} in ${repo_slug} not ready (active=${pending}, blocking_failures=${blockers}, advisory_failures=${advisory}) (GH#27137)" >>"$LOGFILE"
+		return 1
+	fi
+	echo "[pulse-merge] pre-merge snapshot: terminal check set accepted for PR #${pr_number} in ${repo_slug} (advisory_failures=${advisory}) (GH#27137)" >>"$LOGFILE"
+	return 0
+}

+	local pr_number="$2"

+	local activity_json="$4"

+		echo "[pulse-merge] pre-merge snapshot: no successful review-bot gate is bound to the current head for PR #${pr_number} in ${repo_slug} (GH#27137)" >>"$LOGFILE"
+		return 1
+	fi

+		return 1
+	fi
+	return 0
+}

+	local checks_json="$3"
+	local activity_json="$4"
+	local quiet_seconds="${PULSE_MERGE_QUIET_PERIOD_SECONDS:-30}"
+	local now_epoch="${PULSE_MERGE_NOW_EPOCH:-$(date +%s)}" latest_at="" latest_epoch="" age=""

+	[[ "$quiet_seconds" =~ ^[0-9]+$ ]] || quiet_seconds=30
+	latest_at=$(jq -nr --argjson checks "$checks_json" --argjson activity "$activity_json" '[
+		($checks[]?.observed_at // ""), ($activity.latest_at // "")
+	] | map(select(. != "")) | max // ""') || return 1
+	latest_epoch=$(_pmrc_iso_to_epoch "$latest_at") || return 1

If the GraphQL query fails (e.g., due to an invalid token or network error), `.data` will be null. The current logic will silently evaluate `count` to `0` and allow the merge to proceed, bypassing the review threads check. Validate that `.data.repository.pullRequest` is not null before parsing. Additionally, avoid suppressing stderr with `2>/dev/null` or `2>&1` on `jq` to prevent hiding syntax errors.

```suggestion
	if ! printf '%s' "$response" | jq -e '.data.repository.pullRequest != null' >/dev/null; then
		return 1
	fi
	has_next=$(printf '%s' "$response" | jq -r '.data.repository.pullRequest.reviewThreads.pageInfo.hasNextPage // false') || return 1
```

In shell scripts, when defining a fallback path using the HOME environment variable, use the `${HOME:+$HOME/relative/path}` parameter expansion pattern instead of `${HOME:-}/relative/path`. This prevents the path from resolving to a root-level directory (e.g., `/relative/path`) when HOME is unset or empty, avoiding potential permission issues or unintended behavior.

```suggestion
	printf '%s\n' "${AIDEVOPS_CLI_WARNING_FILE:-${AIDEVOPS_DIR:-${HOME:+$HOME/.aidevops}/logs/cli-convergence-warning.txt}}"
```

+#!/usr/bin/env bash
+# SPDX-License-Identifier: MIT
+# SPDX-FileCopyrightText: 2025-2026 Marcus Quinn

+_CLI_LOCK_OWNED=false
+_CLI_PROCESS_TOKEN=""
+_CLI_READ_PID=""
+_CLI_READ_TOKEN=""
+
+_cli_log() {
+	local level="$1"
+	local message="$2"
+	printf '[aidevops-cli:%s] %s\n' "$level" "$message" >&2
+	return 0
+}
+
+_cli_warning_file() {
+	printf '%s\n' "${AIDEVOPS_CLI_WARNING_FILE:-${AIDEVOPS_DIR:-$HOME/.aidevops}/logs/cli-convergence-warning.txt}"
+	return 0
+}
+
+_cli_write_warning() {
+	local message="$1"
+	local warning_file
+	warning_file=$(_cli_warning_file)
+	local warning_dir="${warning_file%/*}"
+	local warning_tmp="${warning_file}.tmp.$$"
+
+	mkdir -p "$warning_dir" 2>/dev/null || return 1
+	printf '%s\n' "$message" >"$warning_tmp" || return 1
+	mv -f "$warning_tmp" "$warning_file" || return 1
+	_cli_log warning "$message"
+	_cli_log warning "Durable remediation notice: $warning_file"
+	return 0
+}
+
+_cli_clear_warning() {
+	local warning_file
+	warning_file=$(_cli_warning_file)
+	rm -f "$warning_file" 2>/dev/null || true
+	return 0
+}
+
+_cli_release_lock() {
+	local lock_dir="${AIDEVOPS_CLI_LOCK_DIR:-${AIDEVOPS_DIR:-$HOME/.aidevops}/locks/cli-launcher.lock}"
+	local owner_pid=""
+	local owner_token=""
+	if [[ "$_CLI_LOCK_OWNED" == "true" && -r "$lock_dir/initialized" ]]; then
+		IFS= read -r owner_pid <"$lock_dir/pid" || owner_pid=""
+		IFS= read -r owner_token <"$lock_dir/command-token" || owner_token=""
+	fi
+	if [[ "$owner_pid" == "$$" && "$owner_token" == "$_CLI_PROCESS_TOKEN" ]]; then
+		rm -f "$lock_dir/initialized" "$lock_dir/pid" "$lock_dir/lstart" "$lock_dir/command-token" 2>/dev/null || true
+		rmdir "$lock_dir" 2>/dev/null || true
+	fi
+	_CLI_LOCK_OWNED=false
+	return 0
+}
+
+_cli_process_lstart() {
+	local pid="$1"
+	local process_lstart=""
+	process_lstart=$(LC_ALL=C TZ=UTC ps -ww -p "$pid" -o lstart= 2>/dev/null || true)
+	process_lstart="${process_lstart#"${process_lstart%%[![:space:]]*}"}"
+	printf '%s\n' "$process_lstart"
+	return 0
+}
+
+_cli_process_command() {
+	local pid="$1"
+	LC_ALL=C TZ=UTC ps -ww -p "$pid" -o command= 2>/dev/null || true
+	return 0
+}
+
+_cli_lock_owner_active() {
+	local lock_dir="$1"
+	local owner_pid=""
+	local owner_lstart=""
+	local owner_token=""
+	local current_lstart=""
+	local current_args=""
+
+	[[ -r "$lock_dir/initialized" && -r "$lock_dir/pid" && -r "$lock_dir/lstart" && -r "$lock_dir/command-token" ]] || return 2
+	IFS= read -r owner_pid <"$lock_dir/pid" || owner_pid=""
+	IFS= read -r owner_lstart <"$lock_dir/lstart" || owner_lstart=""
+	IFS= read -r owner_token <"$lock_dir/command-token" || owner_token=""
+	[[ "$owner_pid" =~ ^[0-9]+$ && -n "$owner_lstart" && -n "$owner_token" ]] || return 1
+	kill -0 "$owner_pid" 2>/dev/null || return 1
+	current_lstart=$(_cli_process_lstart "$owner_pid")
+	current_args=$(_cli_process_command "$owner_pid")
+	[[ "$current_lstart" == "$owner_lstart" && "$current_args" == *"$owner_token"* ]]
+	return $?
+}
+
+_cli_release_reclaim_mutex() {
+	local reclaim_dir="$1"
+	local owner_pid=""
+	local owner_token=""
+	if [[ -r "$reclaim_dir/initialized" ]]; then
+		IFS= read -r owner_pid <"$reclaim_dir/pid" || owner_pid=""
+		IFS= read -r owner_token <"$reclaim_dir/command-token" || owner_token=""
+	fi
+	if [[ "$owner_pid" == "$$" && "$owner_token" == "$_CLI_PROCESS_TOKEN" ]]; then
+		rm -f "$reclaim_dir/initialized" "$reclaim_dir/pid" "$reclaim_dir/lstart" "$reclaim_dir/command-token" 2>/dev/null || true
+		rmdir "$reclaim_dir" 2>/dev/null || true
+	fi
+	return 0
+}
+
+_cli_read_lock_identity() {
+	local lock_dir="$1"
+
+	_CLI_READ_PID=""
+	_CLI_READ_TOKEN=""
+	[[ -r "$lock_dir/pid" ]] && IFS= read -r _CLI_READ_PID <"$lock_dir/pid" || _CLI_READ_PID=""
+	[[ -r "$lock_dir/command-token" ]] && IFS= read -r _CLI_READ_TOKEN <"$lock_dir/command-token" || _CLI_READ_TOKEN=""
+	return 0
+}
+
+_cli_initialize_lock_dir() {
+	local lock_dir="$1"
+	local process_lstart=""
+
+	process_lstart=$(_cli_process_lstart "$$")
+	if [[ -z "$process_lstart" || -z "$_CLI_PROCESS_TOKEN" ]] ||
+		! printf '%s\n' "$$" >"$lock_dir/pid" ||
+		! printf '%s\n' "$process_lstart" >"$lock_dir/lstart" ||
+		! printf '%s\n' "$_CLI_PROCESS_TOKEN" >"$lock_dir/command-token" ||
+		! : >"$lock_dir/initialized"; then
+		rm -f "$lock_dir/initialized" "$lock_dir/pid" "$lock_dir/lstart" "$lock_dir/command-token" 2>/dev/null || true
+		rmdir "$lock_dir" 2>/dev/null || true
+		return 1
+	fi
+	return 0
+}
+
+_cli_acquire_reclaim_mutex() {
+	local reclaim_dir="$1"
+	local grace_seconds="${AIDEVOPS_CLI_RECLAIM_GRACE_SECONDS:-2}"
+	local waited=0
+	local lock_state=0
+	local observed_pid=""
+	local observed_token=""
+	local current_pid=""
+	local current_token=""
+
+	while ! mkdir "$reclaim_dir" 2>/dev/null; do
+		lock_state=0
+		_cli_lock_owner_active "$reclaim_dir" || lock_state=$?
+		if [[ "$lock_state" -eq 0 ]]; then
+			return 1
+		fi
+		if [[ "$waited" -lt "$grace_seconds" ]]; then
+			sleep 1
+			waited=$((waited + 1))
+			continue
+		fi
+		_cli_read_lock_identity "$reclaim_dir"
+		observed_pid="$_CLI_READ_PID"
+		observed_token="$_CLI_READ_TOKEN"
+		lock_state=0
+		_cli_lock_owner_active "$reclaim_dir" || lock_state=$?
+		if [[ "$lock_state" -eq 0 ]]; then
+			return 1
+		fi
+		_cli_read_lock_identity "$reclaim_dir"
+		current_pid="$_CLI_READ_PID"
+		current_token="$_CLI_READ_TOKEN"
+		if [[ "$current_pid" != "$observed_pid" || "$current_token" != "$observed_token" ]]; then
+			waited=0
+			continue
+		fi
+		rm -f "$reclaim_dir/initialized" "$reclaim_dir/pid" "$reclaim_dir/lstart" "$reclaim_dir/command-token" 2>/dev/null || true
+		rmdir "$reclaim_dir" 2>/dev/null || true
+		waited=0
+	done
+
+	_cli_initialize_lock_dir "$reclaim_dir"
+	return $?
+}
+
+_cli_try_reclaim_lock() {
+	local lock_dir="$1"
+	local observed_pid="$2"
+	local observed_token="$3"
+	local observed_initialized="$4"
+	local reclaim_dir="${lock_dir}.reclaim"
+	local current_pid=""
+	local current_token=""
+	local current_initialized=false
+	local lock_state=0
+
+	_cli_acquire_reclaim_mutex "$reclaim_dir" || return 1
+	[[ -r "$lock_dir/pid" ]] && IFS= read -r current_pid <"$lock_dir/pid" || current_pid=""
+	[[ -r "$lock_dir/command-token" ]] && IFS= read -r current_token <"$lock_dir/command-token" || current_token=""
+	[[ -r "$lock_dir/initialized" ]] && current_initialized=true
+	if [[ "$current_pid" != "$observed_pid" || "$current_token" != "$observed_token" || "$current_initialized" != "$observed_initialized" ]]; then
+		_cli_release_reclaim_mutex "$reclaim_dir"
+		return 1
+	fi
+	if [[ "$current_initialized" == "true" ]]; then
+		lock_state=0
+		_cli_lock_owner_active "$lock_dir" || lock_state=$?
+		if [[ "$lock_state" -eq 0 ]]; then
+			_cli_release_reclaim_mutex "$reclaim_dir"
+			return 1
+		fi
+	fi
+	rm -f "$lock_dir/initialized" "$lock_dir/pid" "$lock_dir/lstart" "$lock_dir/command-token" 2>/dev/null || true
+	rmdir "$lock_dir" 2>/dev/null || true
+	_cli_release_reclaim_mutex "$reclaim_dir"
+	return 0
+}
+
+_cli_acquire_lock() {
+	local lock_dir="${AIDEVOPS_CLI_LOCK_DIR:-${AIDEVOPS_DIR:-$HOME/.aidevops}/locks/cli-launcher.lock}"

```suggestion
	current_canonical_branch=$(git -C "$canonical_dir" branch --show-current 2>/dev/null || true)
	local canonical_head=""
	canonical_head=$(git -C "$canonical_dir" rev-parse HEAD 2>/dev/null || true)
```

![medium](https://www.gstatic.com/codereviewagent/medium-priority.svg)

The script checks if `postflight` is executable using `[[ -x "$postflight" ]]`, but then executes it by passing it as an argument to `bash` (`bash "$postflight" --quick`). According to the general rules, when checking for the presence of a script executed via an interpreter, `-f` should be used instead of `-x` because the file does not require the executable bit to be set.

```suggestion
	bash "$postflight" --quick >/dev/null 2>&1 || return 1
```

![medium](https://www.gstatic.com/codereviewagent/medium-priority.svg)

In shell scripts with `set -e` enabled, calling `shift 2` when there is only one argument left (e.g., if a parameter like `--session-key` is passed as the last argument without a value) will cause the script to terminate immediately with a non-zero exit status. To prevent this, validate that there is an argument available before shifting.

```shell
	while [[ $# -gt 0 ]]; do
		local option="${1:-}"
		case "$option" in
		--session-key|--runner-key|--worktree|--branch|--changed-paths|--recoverability)
			if [[ $# -lt 2 ]]; then
				echo "Error: Option $option requires an argument" >&2
				return 1
			fi
			local option_value="$2"
			case "$option" in
			--session-key) session_key="$option_value" ;;
			--runner-key) runner_key="$option_value" ;;
			--worktree) worktree_path="$option_value" ;;
			--branch) branch_name="$option_value" ;;
			--changed-paths) changed_paths="$option_value" ;;
			--recoverability) recoverability="$option_value" ;;
			esac
			shift 2
			;;
		*)
			echo "Error: Unknown option for record-recovery: $option" >&2
			return 1
			;;
			esac
		done
```

<details>
<summary>References</summary>

1. In shell scripts with `set -e` enabled, validate the presence of arguments for all value-taking options before shifting (e.g., using a shared presence check) to ensure the script fails with a clean diagnostic and an explicit exit status (such as 1) instead of abruptly terminating with a shell error.
</details>

![medium](https://www.gstatic.com/codereviewagent/medium-priority.svg)

If `.mergeCommit` is `null` (which can happen if the PR is not merged or in some API states), evaluating `.mergeCommit.oid` will throw a `Cannot index null with string "oid"` error in `jq`. Since stderr is not redirected to `/dev/null` here, this error will pollute the output. Checking the type of `.mergeCommit` first ensures safe evaluation across all `jq` versions.

```suggestion
	if ! printf '%s' "$pr_json" | jq -e '
		def present: ((. // "") | length > 0);
		(.state == "MERGED")
		and (.mergedAt | present)
		and (.mergeCommit | type == "object" and (.oid | present))
	' >/dev/null; then
		return 1
	fi
```

```suggestion
		log_error "Active promotion not found: $memory_id"
		return 1
	fi

	target_file=$(graduated_file_path) || return 1
```

![medium](https://www.gstatic.com/codereviewagent/medium-priority.svg)

Using `shift 2` inside the argument parsing loop without verifying that a second argument exists can cause the script to crash. If `--reason` or `--corrected-by` is passed as the last argument on the command line (with no value following it), `shift 2` will fail when `$#` is 1. Since `set -e` is active, this failure will immediately terminate the script with a shell error instead of showing a clean, user-friendly error message.

We should check if there are at least 2 arguments remaining before performing `shift 2`.

```shell
	while [[ $# -gt 0 ]]; do
		case "$1" in
		--reason)
			if [[ $# -lt 2 ]]; then
				log_error "Option --reason requires an argument"
				return 1
			fi
			reason="$2"
			shift 2
			;;
		--corrected-by)
			if [[ $# -lt 2 ]]; then
				log_error "Option --corrected-by requires an argument"
				return 1
			fi
			corrected_by="$2"
			shift 2
			;;
		*) shift ;;
		esac
	done
```

<details>
<summary>References</summary>

1. In shell scripts with `set -e` enabled, validate the presence of arguments for all value-taking options before shifting (e.g., using a shared presence check) to ensure the script fails with a clean diagnostic and an explicit exit status (such as 1) instead of abruptly terminating with a shell error.
</details>

![medium](https://www.gstatic.com/codereviewagent/medium-priority.svg)

The current implementation performs a linear scan over `$recent_failure_families` for every single `$family` in `$failure_families`, resulting in an $O(N \times M)$ complexity. We can optimize this to $O(N + M)$ by building a lookup map of fingerprints to counts using `reduce` before filtering.

```
      (reduce $recent_failure_families[] as $f ({}; .[$f.fingerprint] = ($f.count // 0))) as $recent_counts
      | [$failure_families[]
        | select((.count // 0) >= $failure_threshold and ($recent_counts[.fingerprint] // 0) >= $failure_threshold and (.confidence // "low") == "high" and (.family // "") != "other-failure")
      ] | length
    )
```

![high](https://www.gstatic.com/codereviewagent/high-priority.svg)

Under `set -eo pipefail`, if `git ls-remote` exits with a non-zero status (which happens when checking for a dereferenced tag `^{}` on a lightweight tag), the subshell assignment will immediately terminate the script. Appending `|| true` inside the subshell ensures that the failure is safely ignored and the fallback logic remains reachable. Also, avoid suppressing stderr with `2>/dev/null` so that actual errors remain visible for debugging.

```suggestion
	release_sha=$(git ls-remote --exit-code --tags origin "refs/tags/v${version}^{}" | cut -f1 || true)
	if [[ -z "$release_sha" ]]; then
		release_sha=$(git ls-remote --exit-code --tags origin "refs/tags/v${version}" | cut -f1 || true)
	fi
```

<summary>References</summary>

1. In shell scripts with 'set -e' enabled, use '|| true' to prevent the script from exiting when a command like 'jq' fails on an optional lookup. Do not suppress stderr with '2>/dev/null' so that actual syntax or system errors remain visible for debugging.
</details>

![medium](https://www.gstatic.com/codereviewagent/medium-priority.svg)

To improve efficiency and avoid redundant API requests, we can check if the issue body or labels already contain a hold pattern before fetching the comments. Since `_der_has_hold` performs a simple substring/regex match, checking the body and labels first allows us to skip the paginated comments fetch entirely when a hold is already declared on the issue itself.

```suggestion
	_der_has_active_status "$labels" && return 0
	_der_has_hold "$body" "" "$labels" && return 0
	comments_json=$(gh api --paginate --slurp "repos/${repo}/issues/${issue_number}/comments?per_page=100" 2>/dev/null) || return 1
```

<summary>References</summary>

1. To improve efficiency and avoid redundant I/O, refactor functions that read and process data to optionally accept pre-computed values as arguments. The function can then skip the data-reading step if the values are provided, while retaining the ability to compute them itself as a fallback.
</details>

![high](https://www.gstatic.com/codereviewagent/high-priority.svg)

Using `jq -e` on a JSONL (JSON Lines) file to check for the existence of a matching record is prone to false negatives. Because `jq` processes each line sequentially, the exit status of `jq -e` is determined solely by the last line processed. If a matching record exists earlier in the file but the last line does not match, `jq -e` will exit with a non-zero status, causing the early return to be skipped and duplicate terminal outcomes to be appended.

To fix this, slurp the file into an array using the `-s` flag and use `any` to check if any element matches the criteria. This ensures the check is robust and independent of the record's position in the file. Additionally, avoid suppressing stderr (e.g., do not use `2>&1` or `2>/dev/null`) so that any syntax or system errors remain visible for debugging.

```suggestion
	if [[ -n "$attempt_id" ]] && jq -e -s --arg aid "$attempt_id" \
		'any(.[] ; .outcome != "pending" and (.attempt_id // "") == $aid)' \
		"$telemetry_file" >/dev/null; then
```

<details>
<summary>References</summary>

1. Avoid suppressing stderr with `2>/dev/null` on commands that parse configuration files (e.g., `jq`), as it can hide syntax errors and make debugging difficult.
</details>

![medium](https://www.gstatic.com/codereviewagent/medium-priority.svg)

The current implementation repeatedly prefixes every single `git` command with `HOME` and `PATH` overrides, which is verbose and error-prone. Additionally, if any command fails, the script exits immediately due to `set -e`, leaving the temporary directory `FIXTURE_ROOT` uncleaned.

We can refactor this to:
1. Use the project's established cleanup pattern (`_save_cleanup_scope`, `trap '_run_cleanups' RETURN`, and `push_cleanup`) to guarantee robust cleanup of the temporary directory under all exit conditions, along with a manual fast-path cleanup at the end.
2. Execute the `git` command sequence inside a subshell `( ... )` where `HOME` and `PATH` are exported, simplifying the commands and improving readability.
3. Use the `-q` flag for `git init` to suppress standard output instead of redirecting to `/dev/null`, ensuring stderr remains visible for debugging.

```shell
_save_cleanup_scope
trap '_run_cleanups' RETURN
FIXTURE_ROOT=$(mktemp -d)
push_cleanup 'rm -rf "${FIXTURE_ROOT}"'
FIXTURE_SHIM_DIR="${FIXTURE_ROOT}/shim"
FIXTURE_HOME="${FIXTURE_ROOT}/home"
FIXTURE_REPO="${FIXTURE_ROOT}/repo"
mkdir -p "${FIXTURE_SHIM_DIR}" "${FIXTURE_HOME}"
cp "${REPO_ROOT}/.agents/scripts/git" "${FIXTURE_SHIM_DIR}/aidevops-git-guard"
if (
	export HOME="${FIXTURE_HOME}"
	export PATH="${FIXTURE_SHIM_DIR}:/usr/bin:/bin"
	FIXTURE_GIT=$(command -v git || true)
	[[ "${FIXTURE_GIT}" != "${FIXTURE_SHIM_DIR}/git" ]] &&
	git config --global --add safe.directory "${FIXTURE_REPO}" &&
	git init -q "${FIXTURE_REPO}" &&
	git -C "${FIXTURE_REPO}" remote add origin "${FIXTURE_ROOT}/upstream.git" &&
	git -C "${FIXTURE_REPO}" config --local gc.auto 0 &&
	git -C "${FIXTURE_REPO}" submodule foreach --recursive true
); then
	check 1 "trusted checkout init/config/remote/submodule fixture bypasses parked guard" ""
else
	check 0 "trusted checkout init/config/remote/submodule fixture bypasses parked guard" "trusted actions/checkout commands did not use the runner Git binary"
fi
rm -rf "${FIXTURE_ROOT}"
```

### Robustness & Portability Improvements for Metadata Check

There are three key areas where `_worktree_metadata_contains_path` can be made significantly more robust:
1. **Error Handling (High Severity)**: If `git worktree list` fails (e.g., due to a repository lock or invalid context), the current process substitution silently ignores the failure because of `|| true`. This causes the function to return `1` (not found), which `prune_missing_worktree_metadata` incorrectly interprets as a successful prune (false positive).
2. **Carriage Returns (Medium Severity)**: On Windows/WSL environments, `git` output may contain carriage returns (`\r`). Stripping them via `tr -d '\r'` ensures exact string matching works reliably.
3. **Trailing Slashes (Medium Severity)**: If `wt_path` contains any trailing slashes, the exact match `[[ "$listed_path" == "worktree $wt_path" ]]` will fail. Stripping trailing slashes from `wt_path` beforehand prevents this.

We can resolve all of these by capturing the output of `git worktree list` into a local variable, checking its exit status, and processing the lines with here-strings. Note that we avoid using `2>/dev/null` to ensure that authentication, syntax, or system issues remain visible for debugging.

```suggestion
_worktree_metadata_contains_path() {
	local real_git="$1"
	local repo_context="$2"
	local wt_path="$3"
	local list_output
	local clean_wt_path="${wt_path%/}"

	list_output=$("$real_git" -C "$repo_context" worktree list --porcelain | tr -d '\r') || return 2

	if [[ -z "$list_output" ]]; then
		return 1
	fi

	local listed_path=""
	while IFS= read -r listed_path; do
		[[ "$listed_path" == "worktree $clean_wt_path" ]] && return 0
	done <<< "$list_output"

	return 1
}
```

<summary>References</summary>

1. Avoid using '2>/dev/null' for blanket suppression of command errors in shell scripts to ensure that authentication, syntax, or system issues remain visible for debugging.
</details>

### Handle Error Status from Metadata Check

Update `prune_missing_worktree_metadata` to handle the new tri-state return status from `_worktree_metadata_contains_path` (0 = found, 1 = not found, 2/other = error). This ensures that any failure to query the git metadata is treated as a failure rather than a false-positive success. Additionally, ensure we add a guard clause to check if `real_git` is empty before using it, and avoid blanket error suppression with `2>&1`.

```shell
prune_missing_worktree_metadata() {
	local repo_context="$1"
	local wt_path="$2"
	local real_git=""
	local check_status

	[[ -n "$repo_context" && -d "$repo_context" && -n "$wt_path" ]] || return 1
	[[ ! -e "$wt_path" ]] || return 1
	real_git=$(_worktree_cleanup_real_git) || return 1
	[[ -n "$real_git" ]] || return 1

	_worktree_metadata_contains_path "$real_git" "$repo_context" "$wt_path"
	check_status=$?
	if [[ $check_status -eq 1 ]]; then
		return 0
	elif [[ $check_status -ne 0 ]]; then
		return 1
	fi

	"$real_git" -C "$repo_context" worktree prune >/dev/null || return 1

	_worktree_metadata_contains_path "$real_git" "$repo_context" "$wt_path"
	check_status=$?
	if [[ $check_status -eq 1 ]]; then
		return 0
	fi

	return 1
}
```

![medium](https://www.gstatic.com/codereviewagent/medium-priority.svg)

Using `jq -es` (slurp) reads the entire telemetry file into memory and parses all entries into a single array before executing the filter. If the telemetry file grows large over time, this can lead to high memory usage and performance degradation.

Instead, we can use `jq -ne` with the `inputs` generator. This allows `jq` to stream the JSONL file line-by-line and short-circuit (exit early) as soon as a matching terminal outcome is found, without loading the entire file into memory. Make sure to verify this change using bash -n, shellcheck, and focused jq -n test cases.

```suggestion
	if [[ -n "$attempt_id" ]] && jq -ne --arg aid "$attempt_id" \
		'any(inputs; .outcome != "pending" and (.attempt_id // "") == $aid)' \
		"$telemetry_file" >/dev/null; then
```

_🎯 Functional Correctness_ | _🟠 Major_ | _⚡ Quick win_

**Fix permission union logic to account for top-level inheritance and preserve explicit `none` permissions.**

The Python script has functional correctness gaps in calculating the required permissions union:

1. **Ignored top-level inheritance**: It only examines job-level `permissions` blocks. In GitHub Actions, jobs without a `permissions` block inherit the workflow's top-level `permissions`. If a reusable workflow relies on top-level permissions, this script will incorrectly assume those jobs require no permissions, leading to an incomplete union.
2. **Dropped `none` permissions**: The comparison `levels[level] > levels.get(..., 0)` drops explicitly requested `none` permissions because `0 > 0` evaluates to `False`. If a reusable workflow explicitly specifies `actions: none`, it is omitted from the `required` union, causing the exact-match assertion (`granted != required`) to incorrectly fail even if the caller perfectly mirrors the reusable workflow.
3. **Empty file vulnerability**: `yaml.safe_load()` returns `None` for empty files, which will crash the script with an `AttributeError` when `.get()` is called.

	fi

The systemd properties `NextElapseUSecRealtime`, `NextElapseUSecMonotonic`, and `LastTriggerUSec` return raw microsecond timestamps (e.g., `1719830400000000`). Printing these raw values directly is not human-readable and degrades the usability of the `status` command.

Since systemd is Linux-specific, we can safely use the GNU `date` command to format these microsecond values into human-readable calendar dates. We should also check if the values are numeric to ensure compatibility with mocked test environments. Note that we avoid suppressing stderr with `2>/dev/null` on the `date` command to ensure any syntax or compatibility issues remain visible for debugging.

```shell
	local next_fire_raw next_fire last_fire_raw last_fire
	next_fire_raw=$(_systemd_unit_property "$timer_unit" "NextElapseUSecRealtime")
	if [[ -z "$next_fire_raw" ]] || [[ "$next_fire_raw" == "0" ]] || [[ "$next_fire_raw" == "n/a" ]]; then
		next_fire_raw=$(_systemd_unit_property "$timer_unit" "NextElapseUSecMonotonic")
		if [[ -n "$next_fire_raw" && "$next_fire_raw" != "0" && "$next_fire_raw" != "n/a" ]]; then
			if [[ "$next_fire_raw" =~ ^[0-9]+$ ]]; then
				next_fire="+$((next_fire_raw / 1000000))s (monotonic)"
			else
				next_fire="$next_fire_raw"
			fi
		fi
	elif [[ -n "$next_fire_raw" ]]; then
		if [[ "$next_fire_raw" =~ ^[0-9]+$ ]]; then
			next_fire=$(date -d "@$((next_fire_raw / 1000000))" "+%Y-%m-%d %H:%M:%S %Z" || echo "$next_fire_raw")
		else
			next_fire="$next_fire_raw"
		fi
	fi
	last_fire_raw=$(_systemd_unit_property "$timer_unit" "LastTriggerUSec")
	if [[ -n "$last_fire_raw" && "$last_fire_raw" != "0" && "$last_fire_raw" != "n/a" ]]; then

		else
			last_fire="$last_fire_raw"
		fi
	fi
```

`git rev-parse --git-path` returns a path relative to the repository's git directory (e.g., `.git/aidevops-permission-pending`). If the script is executed from a different working directory, writing to this relative path will write to the wrong location (or fail if there is no `.git` directory in the current working directory). Using `git rev-parse --absolute-git-dir` ensures we resolve the correct absolute path.

```suggestion
		local git_dir=""
		git_dir=$(git -C "$work_dir" rev-parse --absolute-git-dir 2>/dev/null) || return 1
		local pending_file="${git_dir}/aidevops-permission-pending"
```

The `IN` operator in `jq` is a feature introduced in version 1.6. Using it will cause syntax errors and complete script failure on environments running `jq` 1.5 (which is still common on older LTS distributions and enterprise systems). Replacing it with standard boolean comparisons ensures maximum compatibility.

```suggestion
		| [ .[] | select(.author_association | . == "OWNER" or . == "MEMBER" or . == "COLLABORATOR") ]
```

![medium](https://www.gstatic.com/codereviewagent/medium-priority.svg)

If `git status` fails (e.g., if the directory is not a git repository or git is not installed), the pipeline will return a non-zero exit code. Because `set -eo pipefail` is active, this will cause the entire script to terminate immediately. Appending a fallback `|| printf '[]\n'` ensures the script continues gracefully and returns an empty array.

```suggestion
	git -C "$work_dir" status --short 2>/dev/null \
		| cut -c4- \
		| awk 'NF { print }' \
		| head -20 \
		| jq -Rsc 'split("\n") | map(select(length > 0))' || printf '[]\n'
```

<details>
<summary>References</summary>

1. When executing pipelines in shell scripts where set -eo pipefail is active, ensure that potential failures in the pipeline are handled or guarded (e.g., with a fallback or || true) to prevent premature script termination.
</details>

Using `decode("unicode_escape")` followed by a `latin-1` encoding round-trip is fragile and can lead to runtime crashes. Specifically:\n1. If any input contains a backslash followed by `u` (e.g., a path like `C:\\user` or a passphrase containing `\\utility`), `decode("unicode_escape")` will fail with a `UnicodeDecodeError: truncated \\uXXXX escape`.\n2. If the input contains a valid Unicode escape sequence (like `\\u20ac`), the subsequent `.encode("latin-1")` will fail with a `UnicodeEncodeError` because the character cannot be represented in Latin-1.\n\nTo safely expand standard escape sequences (like `\\n`, `\\r`, `\\t`) while fully preserving raw multi-byte UTF-8 characters and avoiding these crash vectors, use `codecs.escape_decode` on the raw bytes before decoding to UTF-8.


![critical](https://www.gstatic.com/codereviewagent/critical.svg)

By default, Python's `sqlite3` module automatically manages transactions. When you manually execute `BEGIN IMMEDIATE`, the library's internal transaction state tracking is bypassed. On Python versions prior to 3.12, subsequent DML statements (such as `UPDATE` or `DELETE`) will trigger the library to automatically issue another `BEGIN` statement, resulting in a `sqlite3.OperationalError: cannot start a transaction within a transaction`.

To fix this, you must set `isolation_level=None` on the connection to disable automatic transaction management. Additionally, when `isolation_level=None` is active, the `connection.commit()` method becomes a no-op because the library's internal transaction state is not tracked. Therefore, you must explicitly execute `COMMIT` and `ROLLBACK` statements using `connection.execute()` to ensure the transaction is correctly committed or rolled back on failure.

```shell
connection = sqlite3.connect(db_path, isolation_level=None)
try:
    connection.execute("BEGIN IMMEDIATE")
    existing_owner = connection.execute(
        """SELECT owner_pid, COALESCE(owner_session, '')
           FROM worktree_owners WHERE worktree_path = ?""",
        (worktree_path,),
    ).fetchone()
    if (
        existing_owner
        and isinstance(existing_owner[0], int)
        and existing_owner[0] != owner_pid
    ):
        try:
            os.kill(existing_owner[0], 0)
        except OSError:
            connection.execute(
                """DELETE FROM worktree_owners
                   WHERE worktree_path = ? AND owner_pid = ?
                     AND COALESCE(owner_session, '') = ?""",
                (worktree_path, existing_owner[0], existing_owner[1]),
            )

    connection.execute(
        """UPDATE worktree_owners
           SET branch = ?, owner_pid = ?, owner_session = ?, owner_batch = ?,
               task_id = ?, owner_comm = ?, owner_dead_seen_at = ''
           WHERE worktree_path = ?
             AND (owner_pid = ? OR (? AND owner_session = ?))""",
        (
            branch,
            owner_pid,
            session_id,
            batch_id,
            task_id,
            owner_comm,
            worktree_path,
            owner_pid,
            trusted_session,
            session_id,
        ),
    )
    connection.execute(
        """INSERT OR IGNORE INTO worktree_owners
           (worktree_path, branch, owner_pid, owner_session, owner_batch,
            task_id, owner_comm, owner_dead_seen_at)
           VALUES (?, ?, ?, ?, ?, ?, ?, '')""",
        (worktree_path, branch, owner_pid, session_id, batch_id, task_id, owner_comm),
    )
    final_owner = connection.execute(
        """SELECT owner_pid, COALESCE(owner_session, '')
           FROM worktree_owners WHERE worktree_path = ?""",
        (worktree_path,),
    ).fetchone()
    connection.execute("COMMIT")
except Exception:
    try:
        connection.execute("ROLLBACK")
    except sqlite3.OperationalError:
        pass
    raise
finally:
    connection.close()
```

1. When querying SQLite databases within shell scripts, prefer using Python's `sqlite3` module with parameterized queries instead of manual string interpolation or bash-based sqlite3 CLI parameter binding to ensure safety against SQL injection and proper handling of escape characters.
</details>

The current implementation of `_shim_parent_framework_caller` uses a fixed `read -r parent_executable parent_script ignored_args` to parse the parent command. This approach is fragile and fails to correctly identify the script name when:
1. The interpreter is invoked with flags (e.g., `bash -euo pipefail script.sh`), where `parent_script` gets assigned to `-euo` instead of the script.

![medium](https://www.gstatic.com/codereviewagent/medium-priority.svg)

Checking only `[[ -n "$_RELATIONSHIP_EDGE_SEEN_FILE" ]]` does not verify if the temporary file actually exists on the filesystem before attempting to read or write to it. Additionally, under `set -u`, referencing a potentially unset or empty variable directly can lead to unbound variable errors. Use parameter expansion `${_RELATIONSHIP_EDGE_SEEN_FILE:-}` with a file existence check `[[ -f ... ]]` instead. Also, avoid using `2>/dev/null` to suppress errors on file operations if the file's existence has already been verified by a preceding check, as it is redundant and can mask other issues.

```suggestion
_relationship_edge_should_attempt() {
	local blocked_num="$1"
	local blocker_num="$2"
	local edge_key="${blocked_num}|${blocker_num}"
	[[ -f "${_RELATIONSHIP_EDGE_SEEN_FILE:-}" ]] || return 1
	if grep -Fxq -- "$edge_key" "$_RELATIONSHIP_EDGE_SEEN_FILE"; then
		return 1
	fi
	printf '%s\n' "$edge_key" >>"$_RELATIONSHIP_EDGE_SEEN_FILE"
	return 0
}
```

<details>
<summary>References</summary>

1. In Shell scripts with `set -u` or `set -euo pipefail` enabled, referencing a potentially unset variable directly (such as in `[[ ! -f "$VAR" ]]`) will cause an unbound variable error and terminate the script. Use parameter expansion `${VAR:-}` to safely check if the variable is empty or unset before performing file or other checks.
2. Avoid using `2>/dev/null` to suppress errors on file operations if the file's existence has already been verified by a preceding check (e.g., `[[ -f "$file" ]]` or an early return). This practice is redundant for 'file not found' errors and can mask other important issues like permissions problems.
</details>

In Bash, `local` variables are function-scoped rather than block-scoped, so declaring them inside a loop can be misleading. Declaring them at the top of the function is cleaner.

Additionally, to improve efficiency, we should move the calculation of loop-invariant variables outside of the loop. Instead of repeatedly parsing `specific_paths` and computing the basenames inside the loop, we can pre-compute the basenames of `specific_paths` once outside the loop and perform a quick lookup inside the loop.

```shell
_check_tier2_general_paths() {
	local general_paths="$1"
	local specific_paths="$2"
	local pr_basenames="$3"
	local overlap_count="$4"
	local overlapping_files="$5"
	local issue_file specific_file
	local -A specific_basenames

	if [[ -n "$specific_paths" ]]; then
		while IFS= read -r specific_file; do
			[[ -z "$specific_file" ]] && continue
			specific_basenames["${specific_file##*/}"]=1
		done <<<"$specific_paths"
	fi

	if [[ -n "$general_paths" ]]; then
		while IFS= read -r issue_file; do
			[[ -z "$issue_file" ]] && continue
			if [[ -n "${specific_basenames[$issue_file]}" ]]; then

			fi
```

![high](https://www.gstatic.com/codereviewagent/high-priority.svg)

The current regex matches `rel="next"` anywhere in the segment, including inside the URL itself (e.g., if the URL contains `rel=next` as a query parameter). This can lead to incorrect pagination parsing if the actual link relation is different (e.g., `prev` or `first`). To prevent this, parse the parameters section (after the closing `>`) and only check for the `rel="next"` relation there.

```suggestion
		function emit_next(segment, start_at, remainder, end_at, params) {
			start_at = index(segment, "<")
			if (start_at == 0) {
				print invalid
				return 1
			}
			remainder = substr(segment, start_at + 1)
			end_at = index(remainder, ">")
			if (end_at == 0) {
				print invalid
				return 1
			}
			params = tolower(substr(remainder, end_at + 1))
			if (params !~ /(^|[^a-z0-9-])rel[[:space:]]*=[[:space:]]*"?next"?/) return 0
			print substr(remainder, 1, end_at - 1)
			return 1
		}
```

### Performance Optimization: Avoid O(N) GitHub API Calls in a Loop and Consolidate jq Calls

The current implementation of `_verified_worker_closing_pr` performs a `gh pr view` call inside a `while read` loop for every candidate PR returned by `gh pr list`. Since `gh pr list` supports retrieving `closingIssuesReferences` and `mergedAt` directly in its `--json` fields, we can fetch all required data in a single API call.

Additionally, we should consolidate multiple `jq` calls into a single pass to improve performance and script efficiency.

```shell
	local repo_slug="$1"
	local issue_number="$2"
	local branch_name="$3"
```

![medium](https://www.gstatic.com/codereviewagent/medium-priority.svg)

Writing the resolved items to a temporary file `"${PROVENANCE_FILE}.resolved.$$"` is slower due to disk I/O and can leave leftover files if the script is interrupted or crashes before the `rm -f` command is executed. We can capture the output of the pipeline directly into the `resolved_items` variable using command substitution.

```suggestion
	local resolved_items
	resolved_items=$(while IFS= read -r item; do
		resolve_provenance_item "$item" "$current_repository" || true
	done < <(jq -c '.items[]?' "$PROVENANCE_FILE") | jq -sc '.')
	printf '%s\n' "$resolved_items"
```

<details>
<summary>References</summary>

1. When declaring and assigning a local variable in shell scripts, separate the 'local' declaration from the assignment if command substitution is involved, to ensure exit code safety.
2. Before parsing JSON with `jq` in shell scripts, check if the input variable is empty to prevent noisy parse errors. Avoid suppressing stderr with `2>/dev/null` on `jq` so that actual syntax or system errors on non-empty malformed JSON remain visible for debugging.
</details>

![high](https://www.gstatic.com/codereviewagent/high-priority.svg)

In Bash 3.2, owner_pid="$(sh -c 'printf "%s" "$PPID"')" runs sh inside a command substitution subshell. Without an explicit exec, the shell may fork to execute sh rather than exec'ing it directly (especially if there are active traps or depending on the specific Bash 3.2 build/patch level). If it forks, the parent of sh will be the short-lived command substitution subshell itself, rather than the lock-holding shell. Once the command substitution completes, this short-lived subshell PID dies. Any subsequent lock-acquisition attempt by another process will see this PID as dead and prematurely reclaim the lock, breaking mutual exclusion. Using exec guarantees that the command substitution subshell is replaced by the sh process, ensuring its parent is always the lock-holding shell.

```suggestion
		owner_pid="$(exec sh -c 'printf "%s" "$PPID"')" || {
```
